name: Moksy platform services
description: The foundation services: gateway, auth, permissions, projects, requirements, payments, events, jobs, audit.

groups.arch: scorecard row in the Moksy architecture review
groups.gap: gap in the Moksy architecture review
groups.roadmap: roadmap step in the Moksy architecture review

cards.subject: The gateway service
says: is the only public API entry to the Moksy backend
listens on port 5001 in the local stack
is the one service attached to both the public and the internal network
cards.use: need the single door a browser uses to reach the backend
not: sits only on the internal network with no route to the outside

cards.subject: The auth service
says: is described in its package as the token issuer
applies a rank policy that decides which actor may support-as which target
is the proposed publisher of the key set other services would verify tokens against
cards.use: need the service that issues tokens
not: stores the profile record of every user

cards.subject: The users service
says: is described in its package as the user data and persistence service
bumps a tokenVersion when a role or status changes, which invalidates existing JWTs
holds the settings for the email-verification deadline and the lockout policy
cards.use: need the service that stores user records
not: issues the JWTs that every other service verifies

cards.subject: The permissions service
says: is described in its package as the authoritative policy enforcer and RBAC engine
supplies the scope checks that every admin route declares with requirePermission
evaluates the union of scopes carried in the JWT and scopes from assigned roles
cards.use: need the service that decides which scopes a role holds
not: issues the short-lived internal token used between services

cards.subject: The projects service
says: owns the project record that holds one idea and its document
listens on port 5014 in the local stack
has its own dedicated service audit in the docs folder
cards.use: need the service behind the project container for an idea
not: runs the AI interview questions itself

cards.subject: The requirements service
says: runs the interview conversation by generating questions and extracting answers
listens on port 5015 in the local stack
is 54,235 lines, larger than the next three services combined
cards.use: need the service that holds the interview flow
not: synthesises the final document through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint

cards.subject: The preview service
says: listens on port 5019 in the local stack
has six per-target client subclasses for calling other services
is one of the two upstreams the downloads service reads from
cards.use: need the service that sits upstream of downloads next to the requirements report
not: is the public edge that browsers call directly

cards.subject: The storage service
says: listens on port 5022 in the local stack
builds its internal HTTP client with jwt rather than the shared canonical client
is grouped by the curriculum draft with dictionary and downloads under content
cards.use: need the service that holds stored files for the platform
not: keeps the audit trail of owner-group actions

cards.subject: The dictionary service
says: is described in its package as a hybrid static resource hub
persists its resources in the database and caches them on disk
is mapped by the curriculum draft to content and localisation
cards.use: need the service that serves shared static resources and wording
not: issues invoices for the platform

cards.subject: The registry service
says: is only 1,260 lines long
is the proposed home for every service's published OpenAPI document
is grouped by the curriculum draft with progression under quality
cards.use: need the natural place to publish API contracts
not: is the largest service on the platform

cards.subject: The progression service
says: scores multi-track levels from Novice to Sovereign using signals
carries the MOX currency policy
runs both the customer ladder and the worker ladder
cards.use: need the service behind levels and ladders
not: fans events out to notifications and communications

cards.subject: The downloads service
says: hosts the Report Manager engine, whose half the audit calls real
has a downloads half that the audit calls a convincing stub
has 27 routes, 21 of which have no caller anywhere in the app
cards.use: need the service that mixes streaming report exports with stub bundle rows
not: is a thin proxy with no business logic of its own

cards.subject: The orchestrator service
says: backs up Mongo and then applies pending migrations in every service container
listens on port 5018 in the local stack
uses crypto in its own hand-rolled internal HTTP client
cards.use: need the component that runs migrations across all services
not: delivers events to notifications over HTTP

cards.subject: The jobs service
says: listens on port 5029 in the local stack
builds its internal HTTP client with jwt rather than the shared client
is grouped by the curriculum draft with events and the orchestrator under automation
cards.use: need the service for background work on the platform
not: keeps an in-memory map of webhook subscribers

cards.subject: The events service
says: listens on port 5028 in the local stack
keeps its subscriber registry in an in-memory Map
delivers a signal by awaiting an HTTP POST to notifications and communications
cards.use: need the service that fans signals out to subscribers
not: publishes to a durable broker with retry and a dead-letter queue

cards.subject: EVENT_SIGNAL_FAILED
says: is logged when an inline signal delivery from events fails
is followed by a return rather than a retry
leaves no dead-letter entry and no way to replay the signal
cards.use: see the log line that proves a signal was dropped for good
not: is logged when a queued signal is moved to a dead-letter queue

cards.subject: HTTP_REQUEST_COMPLETED
says: is the structured JSON log line written for each finished request
carries the traceId that Loki indexes
is written by every service through the shared logging contract
cards.use: need the log line that every service emits per request
not: is written only by the gateway

cards.subject: The audit service
says: is reached through the gateway's admin audit-log route
is listed as internal in the port map instead of with a port
assigns retention classes to the records it keeps
cards.use: need the service that keeps the platform audit records
not: publishes OpenAPI documents for every service

cards.subject: The audit retention classes
says: keep authentication events for one year
keep payments records for seven years
keep AI events for two years and use two years as the default
cards.use: need how long each kind of audit record is kept
not: keep every record forever with no per-class period

cards.subject: The notifications service
says: listens on port 5025 in the local stack
uses a Redis-backed socket adapter for real-time delivery
is one of the two services the events service POSTs to
cards.use: need the service that pushes real-time notices to users
not: owns the inbound email and SMS webhook routes

cards.subject: The communications service
says: listens on port 5026 in the local stack
validates Twilio signatures on inbound webhook routes
deduplicates inbound email and SMS by provider message id
cards.use: need the service for email, SMS and chat threads
not: pushes socket notices through a Redis adapter

cards.subject: The chat outbox
says: is the ChatOutboxModel inside communications
is the only outbox pattern that exists in the repository today
is the proposed model to generalise into the shared common package
cards.use: need the existing example of an outbox on the platform
not: is the broker that the events service publishes to

cards.subject: The WebhookEvent model
says: records inbound email and SMS webhooks in communications
makes a repeated delivery of the same provider message id harmless
is listed by the communications roadmap as done
cards.use: need the record that makes inbound provider webhooks exactly-once
not: throttles message sends per user

cards.subject: The usage service
says: is mapped by the curriculum draft to usage metering
sits with reporting and the dashboard under data and analytics
is a platform service that meters what is consumed
cards.use: need the service tied to usage metering
not: issues JWTs for the gateway

cards.subject: The payments service
says: listens on port 5008 in the local stack
is the source of truth for money movement, invoices, payouts and checkout transactions
increments the lifetimeSpendUsd signal behind the customer level
cards.use: need the owner of invoices, payouts and checkout transactions
not: is the authoritative owner of plan entitlements

cards.subject: The subscriptions service
says: listens on port 5007 in the local stack
is the authoritative owner of plan entitlements and the current billing period
holds included monthly tokens, consumed tokens and the overage posture
cards.use: need the owner of what a plan lets a customer do
not: is the source of truth for payouts and checkout transactions

cards.subject: Plan entitlements
says: describe what a plan lets the customer do
are owned by subscriptions rather than payments
drift when they are stored in two services at once
cards.use: need to know who owns what a plan allows
not: are the invoices and charges produced by a plan

cards.subject: The token ledger
says: receives a durable usage event for every AI request
is the event log from which the period summary is derived
is the ledger that the snapshot only summarises
cards.use: need the durable record of AI usage events
not: is a fast-read summary of the current period

cards.subject: The subscription snapshot
says: is a fast-read summary of the current period
is only a summary of the event log
holds the quick view subscriptions reads instead of replaying every usage event
cards.use: need the fast view of the current billing period
not: is the durable record written once per AI request

cards.subject: Block mode
says: refuses AI requests once the allowance has run out
turns requests away instead of switching models or charging extra
cards.use: want requests refused when the allowance is used up
not: bills the customer for the extra usage

cards.subject: Downgrade mode
says: switches to cheaper models once the allowance has run out
keeps requests flowing on lower-cost models
cards.use: want the service to continue on a cheaper model after the allowance ends
not: refuses every request after the allowance ends

cards.subject: Overage mode
says: allows requests beyond the allowance
bills the extra usage
cards.use: want to keep serving beyond the allowance and charge for it
not: swaps to cheaper models without billing

cards.subject: Mock billing mode
says: simulates subscriptions and MOX top-ups instantly
is the local billing mode that needs no Stripe test keys
cards.use: want to try billing flows locally with nothing external
not: charges a real card through Stripe

cards.subject: Stripe test mode
says: runs billing against Stripe with test keys
charges no real money
cards.use: want to exercise real Stripe flows without real charges
not: simulates subscriptions without contacting Stripe

cards.subject: The billing rollout status
says: marks the foundation phase as implemented
treats removing duplicate subscription state from payments as a later phase
lists enforcement, invoices from the token ledger and reconciliation as planned, not built
cards.use: need to know which parts of subscription billing are built today
not: records enforcement and reconciliation as already shipped

cards.subject: The ai-llm service
says: runs the synthesis flow, including the final document on Finalise
talks to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
is configured with LLM_BASE_URL and LLM_PRIMARY_MODEL
cards.use: need the service that makes the final synthesis call
not: runs the live interview question generation

cards.subject: The conversation LLM call
says: uses Ollama through its native client
is configured with OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_MODEL and OLLAMA_TIMEOUT_MS
stays on Ollama even when ai-llm is moved to OpenAI
cards.use: need the model call that generates interview questions
not: goes through LLM_BASE_URL like the synthesis flow

cards.subject: The ai-nlp service
says: is described in its package as the authoritative local NLP engine wrapper
checks a static key only on internal calls, with no JWT check
cards.use: need the service that wraps the local NLP engine
not: synthesises the final document

cards.subject: The ai-memory service
says: is started by the full compose profile alongside ai-llm and ai-nlp
accepts any valid internal token
has no caller allow-list in its guard
cards.use: need the AI service that holds memory rather than language or NLP
not: wraps the local NLP engine

cards.subject: The ai-policy service
says: listens on port 5017 in the local stack
accepts any valid internal token
is cited by the curriculum draft as a source for governance and compliance
cards.use: need the service that applies policy to AI use
not: generates interview questions with Ollama

cards.subject: OPENAI_API_KEY set to ollama
says: is set that way on purpose
exists because the ai-llm service expects the variable to be present
must not be left blank
cards.use: wonder why a local setup sets an OpenAI key to a word
not: is a real key that Ollama checks

cards.subject: The JSON-strict reply format
says: is expected by the requirements service from its model
can be broken by very small models under 3 B parameters
produces a graceful fallback and a no question generated message rather than a crash
cards.use: need to explain why a tiny local model yields no question
not: makes the gateway crash when the reply is invalid

cards.subject: The full compose profile
says: activates ai-llm, ai-nlp and ai-memory
also brings up payments, the docs site and tooling sidecars
is what npm run dev starts, unlike a bare docker compose up
cards.use: need to know which services only start with the full profile
not: is what a plain docker compose up starts

cards.subject: The common package
says: publishes the shared error envelope
carries Sentry support
holds the canonical internal HTTP client and guard
cards.use: need the shared library every service is meant to use
not: holds the frontend dashboard code

cards.subject: The canonical internal guard
says: is internalAuth in the common package
accepts only api-gateway as a caller
enforces a 30-second replay window
is used by none of the services
cards.use: need the shared guard that forced services to write their own looser copies
not: accepts any service name that signs a token

cards.subject: The canonical HttpClient
says: carries a failure-threshold circuit breaker
forwards the x-correlation-id header
is used by only one service today
cards.use: need the shared internal client with a circuit breaker
not: is used by every service in place of its own client

cards.subject: The reporting package
says: powers the Report Manager engine hosted by the downloads service
lives in the packages directory rather than among the 25 services
is listed by the curriculum draft under data and analytics
cards.use: need the package behind report export and import
not: holds the pattern registry

cards.subject: The patterns package
says: lives in the packages directory rather than among the 25 services
is listed by the curriculum draft under automation with jobs, events and the orchestrator
cards.use: need the package tied to 1:99 patterns
not: powers the Report Manager

cards.subject: The mcp-server package
says: lives in the packages directory rather than among the 25 services
is listed by the curriculum draft under the AI area with ai-llm, ai-memory and ai-nlp
cards.use: need the shared package for the MCP server
not: powers report exports

cards.subject: The packages directory
says: holds common, knowledge-base, mcp-server, newton-client, patterns, reporting, sdk and zapier-app
sits beside the foundation folder and the apps folder
holds code shared by services and apps
cards.use: need where shared code lives rather than a service
not: holds the 25 backend services

cards.subject: The foundation folder
says: holds the backend services
is where the curriculum draft counted 29 services while the review counts 25
has a Dockerfile and package.json in each service
cards.use: need where the backend services live
not: holds the dashboard and docs frontends

cards.subject: Scorecard row: independent deployment
says: is evidenced by 25 services with their own Dockerfile and package.json
is helped by a deploy script that rebuilds only changed services
cards.use: need the row about deploying one service without the rest
not: is rated red

cards.subject: Scorecard row: database per service
says: is evidenced by 23 distinct logical databases
has one cross-database exception, a one-off backfill script in progression
cards.use: need the row that found no service reading another's collections
not: is rated amber

cards.subject: Scorecard row: private network and single edge
says: depends on moksy-internal being a Docker internal network
leaves only the gateway publishing a port for the API
cards.use: need the row about the network layout
not: is rated red

cards.subject: Scorecard row: health and structured logging
says: finds /health on all 25 services
finds a JSON request log line with a propagated traceId
cards.use: need the row about per-service health endpoints
not: is rated red

cards.subject: Scorecard row: shared error contract
says: rests on the error envelope in the common package
adds Sentry and Loki with promtail indexing traceId
cards.use: need the row about common errors and observability
not: is rated amber
like: Scorecard row: health and structured logging

cards.subject: Scorecard row: authenticated service calls
says: is the only row rated amber
has a handshake of a gateway key plus an internal token JWT
has one shared secret and five divergent implementations
cards.use: need the only amber row in the scorecard
not: is rated green

cards.subject: Scorecard row: encrypted transport
says: finds every hop on plain http
finds zero TLS, zero mTLS and zero service identity
cards.use: need the row about traffic between services being plaintext
not: is rated amber

cards.subject: Scorecard row: asynchronous communication
says: finds no broker on the platform
finds events fanning out inline over HTTP from an in-memory map
cards.use: need the row about decoupled messaging
not: is rated green
like: Scorecard row: services own their logic

cards.subject: Scorecard row: services own their logic
says: points to a 9,577-line gateway controller
finds orchestration and domain rules in the gateway
cards.use: need the row about the gateway holding business logic
not: is rated green

cards.subject: Scorecard row: published contracts
says: finds zero OpenAPI or AsyncAPI files in the repo
leaves every consumer coupled to an undocumented response shape
cards.use: need the row about versioned API contracts
not: is rated green
like: Scorecard row: services own their logic

cards.subject: The 60 percent verdict
says: says the decomposition is real but the contract between services is not
places the platform roughly 60 percent of the way to the goal
concentrates the remaining 40 percent in four places
cards.use: need the review's overall summary of the platform
not: says the platform is a finished microservice architecture

cards.subject: Gap 1: one shared secret
says: makes every service hold every other service's key in practice
uses symmetric HS256, so a verifier can also forge tokens
cannot rotate one service's credential without rotating all
cards.use: see why a compromised service can impersonate any other
not: is solved by replay protection

cards.subject: Gap 2: divergent client and guard copies
says: has 25 hand-written internalAuth copies
uses six competing header names
enforces different rules in different guards
cards.use: see why 25 copies of the guard exist
not: is about plaintext traffic

cards.subject: Gap 3: the x-user header
says: carries the actor as unsigned JSON that services parse
lets anything holding the gateway key assert an admin role
is read by users in eight separate places
cards.use: see why one compromised service can mean platform-wide admin
not: is already a signed short-lived assertion

cards.subject: Gap 4: no transport encryption
says: finds every inter-service URL on plain http
becomes unsurvivable once services span hosts or a managed cluster
is answered by mTLS on every hop
cards.use: see why moving to Kubernetes needs encryption between services
not: is already solved by a service mesh in place

cards.subject: Gap 5: events as inline HTTP fan-out
says: keeps the subscriber registry in process memory
has no queue, no retry, no dead-letter and no replay
is the root cause of a restart killing work in flight
cards.use: see why a restart mid-report loses the work for good
not: is solved by the outbox in communications
like: Gap 6: the gateway as the brain

cards.subject: Gap 6: the gateway as the brain
says: holds about 8,000 lines of orchestration that belong to services
means any domain flow change needs a gateway deploy
makes the gateway the highest-blast-radius component
cards.use: see why a domain change forces a gateway deploy
not: is rated as a small routing layer of about 1,500 lines

cards.subject: Gap 7: no published contracts
says: finds zero OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or schema-registry files
couples consumers to undocumented response shapes
is why return-shape bugs surface that unit tests cannot catch
cards.use: see why wiring work keeps finding return-shape bugs
not: is about the gateway controller size
like: Gap 6: the gateway as the brain

cards.subject: Gap 8: four services on the public network
says: attaches ai-llm, requirements, payments and progression to moksy-public
publishes a host port for progression
suggests a separate egress network for services that call third parties
cards.use: see which services are reachable from outside without needing to be
not: finds the gateway on the internal network only

cards.subject: The replay window finding
says: finds 23 of 25 services accept replayable internal requests
has only auth and users enforcing a replay window
means one captured internal call can be replayed indefinitely
cards.use: see why a captured internal call can be replayed
not: finds that every service enforces a 30-second timestamp window

cards.subject: The requirements size finding
says: puts requirements at 54,235 lines, 3.7 times the gateway
has absorbed the pillar engine, marketplace, experiment harness and catalog
is called a monolith wearing a service's clothes
cards.use: see which service the review says should be decomposed along its seams
not: describes the downloads service as a stub
like: Gap 6: the gateway as the brain

cards.subject: Phase 1: collapse to one implementation
says: makes the common guard accept a configurable caller allow-list
moves all 25 services onto one guard and one client
deletes the per-service copies of both
cards.use: want the roadmap step that needs no new infrastructure
not: introduces a broker

cards.subject: Phase 2: real service identity
says: moves from shared HS256 to per-service RS256 or EdDSA keypairs
has auth publish JWKS
replaces the raw x-user header with a signed actor assertion
cards.use: want the roadmap step about asymmetric service keys
not: installs a service mesh

cards.subject: Phase 3: encrypted transport
says: writes Kubernetes manifests for the other 24 services
installs Linkerd for automatic mTLS
adds default-deny NetworkPolicies per service
cards.use: want the roadmap step about mTLS and manifests
not: moves notifications onto events

cards.subject: Phase 4: genuine decoupling
says: stands up a broker and generalises the outbox
rewrites events as a broker-backed registry with persistence, retry and a DLQ
generates OpenAPI per service and publishes it to registry
cards.use: want the roadmap step that is largest and can run in parallel
not: only consolidates existing guard copies

cards.subject: The header vocabulary freeze
says: cuts six header names down to three
is part of Phase 1
deletes the other three names
cards.use: need the cleanup of x-internal-gateway-key, x-internal-token and their rivals
not: adds a seventh header for service identity

cards.subject: Per-service Mongo users
says: replace every service connecting as the authSource=admin root
are scoped to each service's own database
belong to Phase 2
cards.use: need the step that limits a compromised service's database reach
not: are installed with the service mesh

cards.subject: The broker choice
says: names Redis Streams as the pragmatic option since Redis is already deployed
names NATS JetStream or RabbitMQ as alternatives with stronger durability
notes Redis is used today only for gateway rate-limiting and the notifications socket adapter
cards.use: need which broker the review suggests
not: recommends Kafka as the only option

cards.subject: The three priorities
says: lists Phase 1 in full first
kills the x-user header second
makes events durable third
cards.use: need the review's if-you-only-do-three-things list
not: starts with the Kubernetes mesh

cards.subject: The no-auto-deploy rule
says: means pushing to GitHub does not touch the server
requires SSH, git pull and a deploy command by hand
has no CI/CD pipeline deploying on anyone's behalf
cards.use: want to know what happens after git push
not: deploys the server on every push to main

cards.subject: npm run deploy:prod
says: rebuilds only services whose code changed
runs a post-deploy health check
records the commit in .last-deploy-sha
cards.use: need the normal server deploy command
not: rebuilds every service every time

cards.subject: npm run deploy:prod:plan
says: previews a deploy without touching anything
shows what would be rebuilt
is the safe look before a deploy
cards.use: want to see which services a deploy would rebuild
not: performs the rebuild and restart

cards.subject: npm run deploy:prod:full
says: forces a full rebuild of everything
ignores the changed-services shortcut
cards.use: need a rebuild of all services
not: rebuilds only changed services

cards.subject: How changed services are detected
says: is derived from each Dockerfile's COPY paths
limits a deploy to services whose code changed
needs no manual list of services
cards.use: need how deploy:prod picks what to rebuild
not: compares the commit message to a service name

cards.subject: npm run release
says: pulls the images for a given git sha and health-gates the start
is also how you roll back, by releasing an earlier sha
auto-rolls-back if the new release fails its health check
cards.use: need a deploy from prebuilt images with a rollback path
not: builds images on the server from source

cards.subject: The build-push workflow
says: is workflow_dispatch only and never runs on push
publishes images to ghcr.io/moksy-ai/moksy-<service>:<git-sha>
never deploys anything
cards.use: need the workflow that publishes tagged images
not: deploys to the server on every push

cards.subject: Backup-gated migrations
says: have each service own its migrations
have the orchestrator back up Mongo first
follow expand then contract discipline
cards.use: need how migrations are applied safely across services
not: run automatically on every git push

cards.subject: bootstrap-vps.sh
says: stands up or rebuilds the stack on a clean VPS
can pull pre-built images at a known-good commit with --tag
is backed by a disaster-recovery runbook for durable volumes
cards.use: need to rebuild the platform on a fresh server
not: deploys only changed services on a live server

cards.subject: Loki and Promtail
says: ship logs in the staging and production overlays
index the traceId from the structured log line
cards.use: need the log shipping stack
not: poll health endpoints and send webhook alerts

cards.subject: The alerts sidecar
says: polls service health endpoints
can send webhook alerts
cards.use: need what notifies when a service health check fails
not: ships logs to Loki

cards.subject: Trivy image scanning
says: scans container images locally and in CI
is the scanner named in the image scanning guide
cards.use: need the tool that scans container images
not: rebuilds changed services

cards.subject: A microservice architecture
says: splits a system into independently deployable services
gives each service a narrow responsibility
trades in-process calls for network calls
cards.use: want teams to deploy parts of a system on their own
not: runs all code in one process

cards.subject: A monolith
says: deploys the whole application as one unit
keeps calls in process
is simpler to run than many services
cards.use: need the single-deployable shape
not: gives each feature its own database by default

cards.subject: A distributed monolith
says: has services that must be changed and deployed together
couples services through shared data or one fat orchestrator
pays the network cost of microservices without their independence
cards.use: suspect services are separate in name only
not: is the intended outcome of decomposition

cards.subject: The API gateway pattern
says: gives clients one entry point to many services
handles authentication, rate limiting and routing at the edge
hides internal service topology
cards.use: want a single public door in front of services
not: lets each client call each service directly

cards.subject: Database per service
says: gives each service private data it alone writes
forbids reading another service's tables
forces cross-service data to travel through APIs or events
cards.use: want services loosely coupled through data
not: lets every service read the shared schema

cards.subject: The circuit breaker
says: stops calling a failing dependency after a failure threshold
fails fast while the dependency recovers
probes with a trial call before closing again
cards.use: need to stop a failing dependency dragging down callers
not: retries each failed call forever

cards.subject: Retry with exponential backoff
says: waits longer between each attempt
is often combined with random jitter
is safe only when the operation is idempotent
cards.use: need to retry a flaky call without a stampede
not: retries instantly in a tight loop

cards.subject: An idempotency key
says: lets a client repeat a request without repeating its effect
is sent by the caller and remembered by the server
makes payment and webhook retries safe
cards.use: need a retried request not to charge twice
not: is a signed token proving who the caller is

cards.subject: The transactional outbox
says: writes the state change and the event in one database transaction
has a relay publish the stored events afterwards
avoids the dual-write problem between a database and a broker
cards.use: need a state change and its event to succeed or fail together
not: publishes straight to the broker before committing

cards.subject: The saga pattern
says: splits a distributed transaction into local steps
runs compensating actions when a later step fails
replaces cross-service two-phase commit
cards.use: need a multi-service workflow that can be undone step by step
not: holds one lock across every service until commit

cards.subject: A dead-letter queue
says: holds messages that failed after the retry limit
lets operators inspect and replay failures
keeps a poison message from blocking the queue
cards.use: need somewhere for repeatedly failing messages to go
not: deletes failed messages silently

cards.subject: The bulkhead
says: isolates resources so one failing part cannot exhaust the rest
gives each dependency its own pool of threads or connections
is named after ship compartments
cards.use: need one slow dependency not to consume every worker
not: stops calls after a failure threshold

cards.subject: The strangler fig
says: replaces a legacy system one slice at a time
routes some traffic to new code behind a facade
retires the old code gradually
cards.use: need to migrate a monolith without a big-bang rewrite
not: rewrites the whole system before cutover

cards.subject: A shared symmetric secret
says: lets any holder both sign and verify
cannot be rotated for one party alone when many share it
makes a verifying service able to forge tokens
cards.use: need to explain why one shared key is weak
not: lets a verifier check tokens without being able to forge them

cards.subject: Asymmetric signing
says: signs with a private key and verifies with a public key
lets a verifier check tokens without forging them
underpins RS256 and EdDSA tokens
cards.use: want verification not to imply the power to forge
not: uses one key for both signing and verifying

cards.subject: JWKS
says: is a JSON document publishing public keys
lets callees fetch the keys used to verify tokens
supports key rotation by listing several keys
cards.use: need a standard place to publish token verification keys
not: holds each service's private signing key

cards.subject: Mutual TLS
says: has both client and server present certificates
encrypts traffic and authenticates both ends
gives each workload a verifiable identity
cards.use: need encrypted service traffic where both sides are authenticated
not: only authenticates the server to the client

cards.subject: A service mesh
says: moves mTLS and traffic policy into sidecar proxies
gives service identity without changing application code
can enforce which callers reach which service
cards.use: want mTLS added without every team writing it
not: replaces the database per service rule

cards.subject: Replay protection
says: rejects a captured request that is sent again
often uses a short timestamp window or a nonce
closes the gap left by a valid but old signature
cards.use: need an old captured call not to work again
not: encrypts the request body

cards.subject: A signed actor assertion
says: carries the end user's identity as a signed short-lived claim
is minted by the edge and verified by callees
replaces a free-text user header
cards.use: need services to trust who the original caller was
not: is a JSON header any caller can write

cards.subject: Least privilege
says: gives each identity only the access its job needs
limits the damage of a compromised service
applies to database users as well as roles
cards.use: want a compromised component to reach as little as possible
not: gives every service the admin database user

cards.subject: Zero trust
says: does not trust a request because of the network it came from
verifies identity on every call
assumes the internal network may be compromised
cards.use: want security not to rely on being inside the perimeter
not: trusts anything on the private network

cards.subject: Role-based access control
says: grants permissions through roles
checks a scope or permission per route
is paired with ranks when actors may act as others
cards.use: need permissions grouped by job function
not: grants rights per individual with no roles

cards.subject: Token version revocation
says: invalidates earlier tokens by bumping a counter on the user
takes effect without waiting for tokens to expire
needs each verification to compare the version
cards.use: need a role change to cancel existing JWTs immediately
not: waits for the token expiry to cancel old tokens

cards.subject: Default-deny network policy
says: blocks all traffic unless a rule allows it
lists only declared callers per service
limits lateral movement
cards.use: want only declared callers to reach a service
not: allows everything unless a rule blocks it

cards.subject: A message broker
says: sits between producers and consumers
stores messages until consumers take them
decouples sender availability from receiver availability
cards.use: need sender and receiver not to be up at the same time
not: calls the receiver directly and waits

cards.subject: Redis Streams
says: is an append-only log type inside Redis
supports consumer groups and acknowledgements
persists entries so they can be replayed
cards.use: need a lightweight durable stream where Redis already runs
not: is a pub/sub that drops messages with no subscriber

cards.subject: At-least-once delivery
says: never loses a message but may deliver it twice
needs consumers to be idempotent
is the common default guarantee
cards.use: need to know what retried delivery implies for consumers
not: guarantees exactly one delivery every time

cards.subject: An idempotent consumer
says: handles a repeated message without repeating its effect
often records processed message ids
makes duplicate deliveries harmless
cards.use: need duplicate deliveries to be safe
not: assumes every message arrives only once

cards.subject: Eventual consistency
says: lets replicas or services agree after a delay
accepts that reads may briefly be stale
follows from asynchronous events across services
cards.use: need to explain stale reads after an async update
not: guarantees every read sees the latest write

cards.subject: An append-only ledger
says: records changes as new rows rather than editing old ones
lets a balance be derived by replaying entries
gives an audit-friendly history
cards.use: need money or usage history that cannot be silently rewritten
not: overwrites a running total in place

cards.subject: A materialised snapshot
says: stores a precomputed summary of an event log
speeds up reads
can be rebuilt from the log
cards.use: need fast reads over a long history
not: is the source of truth, not a derived view

cards.subject: A retention policy
says: states how long each kind of data is kept
may differ by class such as payments or logs
ends with deletion or archiving
cards.use: need rules for how long records live
not: keeps all data forever by default

cards.subject: Expand then contract migration
says: adds the new shape alongside the old first
moves readers and writers across before removing the old shape
lets old and new code run during a deploy
cards.use: need a schema change that is safe for rolling deploys
not: drops the old column in the same step as adding the new one

cards.subject: A correlation ID
says: is passed along every hop of a request
lets logs from many services be joined
is forwarded in a header
cards.use: need to follow one request across services
not: identifies a user's account

cards.subject: Structured logging
says: writes logs as machine-readable fields such as JSON
makes logs searchable by field
pairs with a shipping stack
cards.use: want logs that a tool can query
not: writes free-form sentences only

cards.subject: A readiness probe
says: says whether a service is ready to receive traffic
may fail while dependencies are down
is separate from a liveness check
cards.use: need to hold traffic until a service is ready
not: restarts a hung process

cards.subject: A liveness probe
says: says whether a process is alive
triggers a restart when it fails
does not judge whether dependencies are healthy
cards.use: need a hung process restarted automatically
not: holds traffic while dependencies recover

cards.subject: Distributed tracing
says: records a tree of timed spans across services
shows where latency is spent
uses a trace identifier carried across hops
cards.use: need to see where one request spent its time
not: counts requests per second only

cards.subject: A health-gated deploy
says: checks service health after restart before calling the deploy good
reports a failed deploy rather than recording it
can roll back when the check fails
cards.use: want a bad release caught before it is recorded
not: records success as soon as containers start

cards.subject: A canary release
says: sends a small share of traffic to the new version first
compares health before widening
limits blast radius
cards.use: want to test a release on a few users
not: switches all traffic at once

cards.subject: OpenAPI
says: describes synchronous HTTP APIs in a machine-readable file
can be generated from route definitions
supports client generation and contract tests
cards.use: need a published description of a REST API
not: describes asynchronous event channels

cards.subject: AsyncAPI
says: describes event and message channels
documents message payloads and brokers
is the event counterpart to OpenAPI
cards.use: need a published description of events
not: describes synchronous REST routes only

cards.subject: A consumer-driven contract test
says: records what a consumer expects from a provider
is run against the provider in CI
catches return-shape breaks that unit tests miss
cards.use: need to catch an API shape change before it breaks a caller
not: only tests the provider with its own fixtures

cards.subject: A backward-compatible change
says: adds optional fields without breaking existing consumers
avoids removing or renaming fields
lets old and new clients coexist
cards.use: need to change an API without breaking callers
not: renames a field that callers read

cards.subject: Semantic versioning
says: uses major, minor and patch numbers
signals a breaking change with a major bump
applies to packages and APIs
cards.use: need version numbers that say how risky an upgrade is
not: numbers releases by date only

cards.subject: API rate limiting
says: caps how many requests a caller may make in a window
protects a service from overload
is commonly enforced at the gateway
cards.use: need a caller not to flood an API
not: is the same as authentication

cards.subject: A schema registry
says: stores versioned schemas for messages
checks new versions for compatibility
lets producers and consumers agree on a shape
cards.use: need versioned message shapes in one place
not: stores the messages themselves

qa.q: Which Moksy service is the only public API entry?
qa.right: The gateway
qa.why: Everything else sits on the internal Docker network; only the gateway is public, on port 5001 locally.

qa.q: What does Moksy's internal Docker network give the backend services?
qa.right: No route to or from the host, so they are reached only through the gateway
wrong: Automatic TLS between every pair of services
A shared database with all other services
qa.why: moksy-internal is a Docker internal network; only the gateway straddles it and the public network.

qa.q: How many backend services does the architecture review count in the foundation folder?
qa.why: The review scopes 25 backend services, 2 frontends and 3 shared packages.

qa.q: What does the Moksy architecture review say about how far the platform is on the way to a proper microservice architecture?
qa.right: Roughly 60 percent
wrong: It does not give a figure
qa.why: The decomposition is real, the contract between services is not; the verdict is roughly 60 percent.

qa.q: Which service owns plan entitlements in Moksy?
qa.right: Subscriptions
qa.why: Subscriptions is the authoritative owner of entitlements and the billing period; payments owns money movement.

qa.q: Which service is the source of truth for invoices, payouts and checkout transactions?
qa.right: Payments
qa.why: Payments owns money movement; it does not own plan entitlements.

qa.q: Does pushing to GitHub deploy Moksy to the server?
qa.right: No, deployment is a manual step run on the server
wrong: Yes, a pipeline deploys every push to main
Yes, but only for the gateway
Yes, after a manual approval in GitHub
qa.why: There is no auto-deploy: SSH in, git pull, then run the deploy command.

qa.q: What must every Moksy service expose so a deploy can tell it came up?
qa.right: A health endpoint
qa.why: /health is present on all 25 services.

qa.q: What is a microservice architecture?
qa.right: A system split into independently deployable services with narrow responsibilities
wrong: One application deployed as a single unit
A set of functions inside one process
qa.why: Independent deployment and narrow responsibility are the defining traits.

qa.q: What is the job of an API gateway?
qa.right: To give clients a single entry point and handle edge concerns such as routing and authentication
qa.why: A gateway hides internal topology behind one door.

qa.q: Which Moksy service is shown in the port map as internal, with its health check reached through the gateway's admin audit-log route?
qa.right: Audit
qa.why: The port map lists audit as internal and points at the gateway admin audit-log route.

qa.q: What does a role or status change do to a Moksy user's existing JWTs?
qa.right: Invalidates them immediately by bumping tokenVersion
wrong: Re-issues them automatically to the browser
qa.why: The users service bumps tokenVersion so older tokens fail.

qa.q: Which Moksy local billing mode charges no real money and simulates subscriptions instantly, without Stripe keys?
qa.right: Mock mode
qa.why: Billing has mock mode and Stripe test mode; neither charges real money.

qa.q: Which Moksy service keeps its subscriber registry in an in-memory Map?
qa.right: Events
qa.why: EventsService holds this.webhooks = new Map(), which dies on restart.

qa.q: How does Moksy's events service deliver a signal today?
qa.right: By awaiting an HTTP POST to notifications and communications inline
wrong: By writing to a Redis Stream with consumer groups
By publishing to a RabbitMQ queue
qa.why: There is no queue, retry, dead-letter or replay.

qa.q: What does the circuit breaker pattern do?
qa.right: Stops calling a failing dependency after a failure threshold, then probes before resuming
qa.why: It fails fast to protect callers while the dependency recovers.

qa.q: What is the idea behind database per service?
qa.right: Each service owns private data and others reach it only through APIs or events
wrong: All services share one schema for easy joins
Every table gets its own server
Only the gateway has a database
qa.why: It keeps services loosely coupled through data.

qa.q: Why do both a liveness probe and a readiness probe exist?
qa.right: Liveness says whether to restart a process; readiness says whether to send it traffic
wrong: They are two names for the same check
Liveness blocks traffic while dependencies recover
qa.why: A process can be alive but not ready.

qa.q: Why is an idempotency key sent with a payment request?
qa.right: So a retried request does not repeat its effect
qa.why: The server remembers the key and returns the original result.

qa.q: Which Moksy shared package holds the canonical internal HTTP client and guard?
qa.right: The common package
qa.why: The common package publishes the HttpClient and the internal request guard.

qa.q: Moksy keeps plan entitlements in subscriptions and money movement in payments. Why does the platform design insist on this split?
qa.right: When both are stored in two services they drift, so each fact needs one owner
wrong: It lowers the cost of each request
qa.why: One owner per fact avoids drift between copies.

qa.q: What does Moksy's token ledger record?
qa.right: A durable usage event for every AI request
qa.why: The event log is the ledger; the subscription's period snapshot only summarises it.

qa.q: Which statement about the subscription snapshot is true?
qa.right: It is a fast-read summary of the current period, not the source of truth
wrong: It is the durable record of every AI request
qa.why: The ledger holds events; the snapshot summarises them.

qa.q: How long does the Moksy audit service keep payments records, per its retention classes?
qa.right: Seven years
qa.why: Authentication events one year, payments seven, AI events two, two-year default.

qa.q: Which Moksy service is described as the authoritative policy enforcer and RBAC engine?
qa.right: Permissions
qa.why: The auth service issues tokens; permissions enforces policy.

qa.q: What is the Moksy review's rating of authenticated service-to-service calls?
qa.right: Amber
qa.why: A handshake exists, but there is one shared secret and five divergent implementations.

qa.q: Which scorecard rows does the Moksy review rate red?
qa.right: Encrypted transport, asynchronous communication, services owning their logic and published contracts
wrong: Independent deployment, database per service and health
qa.why: Four rows are red; five are green and one amber.

qa.q: What does replay protection stop?
qa.right: A captured valid request being sent again later
wrong: A service being called by the wrong caller name
Traffic being read on the wire
A database being queried by two services
qa.why: A short timestamp window or nonce makes old requests fail.

qa.q: What does JWKS provide?
qa.right: A published set of public keys callees can use to verify tokens
wrong: A list of each service's private keys
qa.why: It supports asymmetric verification and key rotation.

qa.q: What does the transactional outbox solve?
qa.right: The dual write between a database and a broker
qa.why: The state change and the event are stored in one transaction and published afterwards.

qa.q: Why does a local Moksy setup set OPENAI_API_KEY to the word ollama?
qa.right: The ai-llm service expects the variable to exist, and Ollama ignores its value
wrong: Ollama requires that exact key to authenticate
It switches ai-llm to a hosted model
It is a placeholder that must be replaced before first start
qa.why: Leaving it blank is wrong; the value is intentional.

qa.q: A Moksy developer finishes a change to payments only. What should they run on the server after git pull?
qa.right: npm run deploy:prod, which rebuilds only changed services
wrong: npm run deploy:prod:full to rebuild everything every time
Nothing, the push already deployed it
docker compose down on the whole stack
qa.why: deploy:prod builds only the services whose Dockerfile COPY paths changed, then health-checks.
qa.code:
git pull origin main
npm run deploy:prod

qa.q: A developer wants to see what a deploy would rebuild without touching the server. What should they run?
qa.right: npm run deploy:prod:plan
qa.why: The plan command previews the deploy without changing anything.

qa.q: A release from the Moksy registry fails its health check. What does the release script do?
qa.right: Rolls back automatically to the previously recorded good tag
wrong: Leaves the new version running and sends an email
Deletes the images from the registry
qa.why: release.sh records the previous good tag and auto-rolls-back.

qa.q: A Moksy service restarts while the events service is in the middle of delivering a signal. What happens to that signal?
qa.right: It is lost, because events has no queue, retry, dead-letter or replay
wrong: It is retried from a Redis Stream
It is moved to a dead-letter queue
It is replayed by the orchestrator
qa.why: The subscriber map is in memory and delivery is inline.

qa.q: A team adds a service that calls ai-llm. The call returns 403 and silently falls back to env-only config. What does the architecture review say causes this?
qa.right: The canonical guard accepts only api-gateway as caller, so true service-to-service calls are rejected
wrong: ai-llm has run out of tokens
The service lacks a health endpoint
qa.why: That limitation is why services wrote their own looser copies of the guard.

qa.q: A compromised Moksy service sends this header to users. What does it allow?
qa.right: Acting as an admin, because the actor header is unsigned
wrong: Nothing, because the header is verified
Only impersonating other services, not users
qa.why: The review's Gap 3: the actor travels as unsigned JSON, so one compromised service can mean platform-wide admin.

qa.q: A developer sees this in a service's guard. What does the review say about it?
qa.right: It trusts an unsigned header, which the target design replaces with a signed short-TTL actor assertion
wrong: It is verified by auth with a JWKS
qa.why: Never trust a free-text header for identity.

qa.q: A team wants services to verify each other's tokens without being able to forge them. What do they move to?
qa.right: Per-service asymmetric keypairs with auth publishing a JWKS
wrong: Hiding the secret in an environment file
qa.why: Verification stops implying forgery capability.

qa.q: A product owner asks why a domain change needs a gateway deploy. What is the structural reason?
qa.right: The 9,577-line gateway controller holds business orchestration that belongs to services
wrong: The gateway has the only database
The gateway is the only service with Docker
qa.why: Gap 6: about 8,000 lines belong in the owning services.

qa.q: Billing must move a customer to cheaper models when the monthly token allowance is used up, without refusing requests. Which enforcement mode is that?
qa.right: Downgrade
qa.why: The three modes are block, downgrade to cheaper models, and allow overage and bill.

qa.q: A team stores plan limits in both payments and subscriptions and they now disagree. What should they do?
qa.right: Pick one authoritative owner, subscriptions, for entitlements and remove the copy
wrong: Add a nightly job to overwrite both
Store a third copy in the gateway
Allow either to win depending on the request
qa.why: One owner per fact is the design rule.

qa.q: A tiny local model leaves Moksy with a no-question-generated message but no crash. What does the README suggest?
qa.right: Use a 7 B+ model, because very small models can break the JSON-strict reply format
qa.why: The requirements service falls back gracefully when the reply is not strict JSON.

qa.q: Someone proposes Redis Streams as Moksy's first durable broker. Why does the review call it the pragmatic choice?
qa.right: Redis is already deployed and used only for gateway rate-limiting and the notifications socket adapter
wrong: It replaces the database per service rule
It is the only broker that supports retries
qa.why: NATS JetStream or RabbitMQ are alternatives if stronger durability is wanted.

qa.q: Why does the review say 23 of 25 services accept replayable internal requests?
qa.right: Only auth and users enforce the 30-second timestamp window
wrong: The shared secret is rotated hourly
Only 23 services have a health endpoint
qa.why: Capturing one internal call lets it be replayed indefinitely elsewhere.

qa.q: After consolidating the guard (Phase 1), why does the review say later fixes get cheaper?
qa.right: Every later change becomes a one-package change instead of a 25-service change
wrong: The broker removes the need for auth
qa.why: One guard and one client make every later phase a single-place change.

qa.q: A reviewer asks why the downloads service cannot simply be called a stub. What does the audit say?
qa.right: It is two products in one process: a real Report Manager half and a stub downloads half
wrong: It is the gateway under another name
qa.why: 21 of its 27 routes have no caller.

qa.q: A team wants to follow the review's three-things list. What is the right order?
qa.right: Phase 1 in full, then kill the x-user header, then durable events
wrong: Durable events, then Phase 1, then x-user
Service mesh, then broker, then Phase 1
qa.why: The list starts with consolidation.

qa.q: A provider delivers the same inbound SMS webhook to Moksy twice. What prevents a double message?
qa.right: A WebhookEvent record in communications deduplicates by provider message id
qa.why: Inbound email and SMS are deduplicated exactly once by provider message id.

qa.q: A team renames a response field that other services read and calls it a backward-compatible change. What is wrong?
qa.right: Renaming breaks existing consumers; compatible changes add optional fields
qa.why: Removing or renaming fields breaks callers.

qa.q: A service mesh gives mTLS. Why does the roadmap keep the Phase 2 JWTs on top of it?
qa.right: The mesh authenticates workloads while the JWTs remain the authorisation layer
wrong: The JWTs replace the mesh later
JWTs are required for health checks
qa.why: The mesh handles authentication of the transport; tokens still say who may do what.
